clue.text: Time in Channel island is bleak

indicators.note: in tells us the time abbreviation sits inside the island's name

parts.note: Sark is one of the Channel Islands

explanation.surface: A spell on a Channel island is a dreary experience.
explanation.walkthrough: SARK is a small island in the Channel Islands, between England and France.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a stark landscape is bare, harsh and desolate.

clue.text: Readily imbibing a litre in bar

indicators.note: imbibing means drinking in, so the word for readily takes the other letters inside it

parts.note: readily in the sense 'I'd as soon go', meaning willingly, gives soon

explanation.surface: Someone in a pub happily downing a litre of drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Readily' is SOON as in 'I would just as soon' (willingly), not quickly.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a saloon is a room or establishment selling drinks, as in a saloon bar.

clue.text: A later idea Mad Hatter fought

indicators.note: Mad describes the following words as crazed, so their letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Alice's Mad Hatter got into a fight, as a belated thought.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mad' reads as the Hatter's title from Alice in Wonderland, but it is the anagram signal for HATTER FOUGHT.
explanation.definitionFit: Definition by description: a notion that occurs to you only after the event.

clue.text: What helps one remember to stock rice wine

parts.note: to stock goods is to keep them for sale
sake is Japanese rice wine

explanation.surface: A memory trick for remembering to stock up on sake.
explanation.definitionFit: Description: a memento kept to recall a person, place or event.

clue.text: Quickly stop work in Post Office

indicators.note: in places the word for a break from work inside the postal abbreviation

parts.note: to stop work is to rest

explanation.surface: A demand that postal staff down tools without delay.
explanation.walkthrough: PRESTO is a musical term meaning at a fast tempo.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym from music and magic: presto means fast or at once.

clue.text: Keep quiet about a Persian ruler

indicators.note: about means going round, so the call for silence wraps around the article

parts.note: shh is the command to keep quiet

explanation.surface: Advice to say nothing concerning a Persian monarch.
explanation.definitionFit: Title: the shah was the hereditary monarch of Iran, formerly Persia.

clue.text: Went along with a deadly sin

parts.note: greed (avarice) is one of the seven deadly sins

explanation.surface: Someone who gave in to one of the seven deadly sins.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to go along with a proposal is to consent to it.

clue.text: No one from space is real thing, unfortunately

indicators.note: unfortunately suggests things have gone wrong, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A sad admission that genuine aliens do not exist.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition reads as part of a sentence about aliens; it means a person not from outer space.
explanation.definitionFit: Description: in science fiction a human native of our planet, as opposed to an alien.

clue.text: Hold up in one country military establishment

parts.note: the Roman numeral I stands for one

indicators.note: in places the word for delay inside the other letters

parts.note: a nation is a country
to hold up is to delay, to stall

explanation.surface: A robbery taking place in a single country.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: an installation is a base or facility of the armed forces.

clue.text: Machine for turning articles in France and here

parts.note: la is a French definite article
the is the English definite article, the article used here

explanation.surface: A workshop tool described with articles from two countries.
explanation.walkthrough: 'articles' covers both pieces: LA is one in France, THE is one here.
explanation.definitionFit: Description: a lathe spins a workpiece so it can be shaped by cutting tools.

clue.text: Quickly running past those

indicators.note: running suggests movement and disorder, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone sprinting past a group of people at speed.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to go somewhere with all possible speed.

clue.text: Eccentric old king losing head

indicators.note: losing head means the first letter of the king's name is removed

parts.note: Cnut (Canute) was an eleventh-century king of England

explanation.surface: A crazy ancient monarch who was beheaded.
explanation.walkthrough: CNUT, also spelt Canute, ruled England, Denmark and Norway.
explanation.definitionFit: Informal synonym: a nut is a crazy or odd person.

clue.text: Idea so far is to change given expression earlier?

indicators.note: to change tells us the preceding letters are to be altered into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone wondering if an idea needs to change after being stated before.
explanation.definitionFit: Paraphrase: aforesaid describes something already mentioned or stated earlier.

clue.text: Former beer is a seller abroad

parts.note: ex means former
porter is a dark beer

explanation.surface: A one-time beer now sold overseas.
explanation.definitionFit: Description: an exporter sends goods out for sale in other countries.

clue.text: March could feature this bird before tons in September

parts.note: a goose is a bird

indicators.note: in puts the abbreviation for tons inside the abbreviated month

parts.note: Sep is the abbreviation for September

explanation.surface: Wondering whether March could include a bird before autumn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'March' looks like the month beside September, but it is a soldier's stiff-legged parade step.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a goose-step is a stiff, straight-legged style of marching.

clue.text: Some sugar, licorice and another pungent flavouring

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A list of strong flavours in cooking or confectionery.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: garlic is a strong-smelling bulb used to flavour food, like licorice another strong taste.

clue.text: Root Internet Protocol under change of direction

indicators.note: in a down clue, under places the protocol letters below the other piece

parts.note: a turn is a change of direction

explanation.surface: Computer networking jargon about rerouting traffic.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a turnip is a root vegetable.

clue.text: Allergy regularly does for part of the body

indicators.note: regularly means taking every other letter of the word

explanation.surface: An allergy that frequently affects the body.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a leg is a limb, one part of the human frame.

clue.text: Ship having good passage

parts.note: an alley is a narrow passage

explanation.surface: A vessel enjoying a smooth voyage.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a galley is a low, oared ship of ancient times.

clue.text: Doctor concerned with substance not entirely uncommon

parts.note: re means about, concerning
the gist is the substance of something

indicators.note: not entirely means the last letter of the word is dropped

parts.note: rare means uncommon

explanation.surface: A doctor worried about a fairly rare substance.
explanation.walkthrough: In British hospitals a registrar is a doctor ranking below a consultant.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: in the UK a registrar is a senior hospital doctor in training.

clue.text: Indifferent beginning to operation after distress call

indicators.note: after places the first letter following the call

parts.note: SOS is the Morse distress signal

indicators.note: beginning to picks out the first letter of the following word

explanation.surface: An emergency signal sent as a mission begins.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: so-so means middling, neither good nor bad.

clue.text: Fabric made from odd bits of tow, poor in quality

indicators.note: odd bits means the first and third letters of the word

parts.note: ill can mean poor or bad, as in ill-made

explanation.surface: Cheap cloth woven from scraps of rope fibre.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: twill is a cloth woven with diagonal ribs.

clue.text: More than just the colon during exam in English?

parts.note: in means during, as in 'in the night'
a test is an exam

explanation.surface: Questions about punctuation beyond the colon in an English exam.
explanation.walkthrough: 'colon' seems to be punctuation in an English exam; it is the bowel.
explanation.definitionFit: Description: the gut includes the colon and much more, the whole digestive tube.

clue.text: Far from stiff from marathon, perhaps, west of New York

indicators.note: in an across answer, west of puts the race to the left of the city letters

parts.note: a marathon is an example of a run

explanation.surface: A runner's legs are anything but stiff after the New York Marathon.
explanation.definitionFit: Antonym phrasing: runny means fluid, the opposite of stiff.
